question.prompt: What is the smallest whole number larger than the perimeter of any triangle with a side of length \( 5\) and a side of length \(19?\)

solutions.explanation:
Let \(x\) be the third side length. The triangle inequalities give
\[
19-5<x<19+5,
\]
so \(14<x<24\). Both endpoints are excluded because equality would make the triangle flat.

The perimeter is therefore
\[
5+19+x=24+x<48.
\]
Thus \(48\) is larger than every possible perimeter. To show it is the smallest such whole number, choose \(x=23.5\). This is an allowed third side because \(14<23.5<24\), and its perimeter is \(47.5\). Consequently, \(47\) and every smaller whole number fail to exceed every possible perimeter.

The answer is \(\boxed{48}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
solutions.title: Bound the third side
